title: UK companies need more effective boards of directors
titleCn: UK companies need more effective boards of directors
subject: reading

paragraphs.text: UK companies need more effective boards of directors

After a number of serious failures of governance (that is, how they are managed at the highest level), companies in Britain, as well as elsewhere, should consider radical changes to their directors' roles. It is clear that the role of a board director today is not an easy one. Following the 2008 financial meltdown, which resulted in a deeper and more prolonged period of economic downturn than anyone expected, the search for explanations in the many post-mortems of the crisis has meant blame has been spread far and wide. Governments, regulators, central banks and auditors have all been in the frame. The role of bank directors and management and their widely publicised failures have been extensively picked over and examined in reports, inquiries and commentaries.

The knock-on effect of this scrutiny has been to make the governance of companies in general an issue of intense public debate and has significantly increased the pressures on, and the responsibilities of, directors. At the simplest and most practical level, the time involved in fulfilling the demands of a board directorship has increased significantly, calling into question the effectiveness of the classic model of corporate governance by part-time, independent non-executive directors. Where once a board schedule may have consisted of between eight and ten meetings a year, in many companies the number of events requiring board input and decisions has dramatically risen. Furthermore, the amount of reading and preparation required for each meeting is increasing. Agendas can become overloaded and this can mean the time for constructive debate must necessarily be restricted in favour of getting through the business.

Often, board business is devolved to committees in order to cope with the workload, which may be more efficient but can mean that the board as a whole is less involved in fully addressing some of the most important issues. It is not uncommon for the audit committee meeting to last longer than the main board meeting itself. Process may take the place of discussion and be at the expense of real collaboration, so that boxes are ticked rather than issues tackled.

A radical solution, which may work for some very large companies whose businesses are extensive and complex, is the professional board, whose members would work up to three or four days a week, supported by their own dedicated staff and advisers. There are obvious risks to this and it would be important to establish clear guidelines for such a board to ensure that it did not step on the toes of management by becoming too engaged in the day-to-day running of the company. Problems of recruitment, remuneration and independence could also arise and this structure would not be appropriate for all companies. However, more professional and better-informed boards would have been particularly appropriate for banks where the executives had access to information that part-time non-executive directors lacked, leaving the latter unable to comprehend or anticipate the 2008 crash.

One of the main criticisms of boards and their directors is that they do not focus sufficiently on longer-term matters of strategy, sustainability and governance, but instead concentrate too much on short-term financial metrics. Regulatory requirements and the structure of the market encourage this behaviour. The tyranny of quarterly reporting can distort board decision-making, as directors have to 'make the numbers' every four months to meet the insatiable appetite of the market for more data. This serves to encourage the trading methodology of a certain kind of investor who moves in and out of a stock without engaging in constructive dialogue with the company about strategy or performance, and is simply seeking a short-term financial gain. This effect has been made worse by the changing profile of investors due to the globalisation of capital and the increasing use of automated trading systems. Corporate culture adapts and management teams are largely incentivised to meet financial goals.

Compensation for chief executives has become a combat zone where pitched battles between investors, management and board members are fought, often behind closed doors but increasingly frequently in the full glare of press attention. Many would argue that this is in the interest of transparency and good governance as shareholders use their muscle in the area of pay to pressure boards to remove underperforming chief executives. Their powers to vote down executive remuneration policies increased when binding votes came into force. The chair of the remuneration committee can be an exposed and lonely role, as Alison Carnwath, chair of Barclays Bank's remuneration committee, found when she had to resign, having been roundly criticised for trying to defend the enormous bonus to be paid to the chief executive; the irony being that she was widely understood to have spoken out against it in the privacy of the committee.

The financial crisis stimulated a debate about the role and purpose of the company and a heightened awareness of corporate ethics. Trust in the corporation has been eroded and academics such as Michael Sandel, in his thoughtful and bestselling book What Money Can't Buy, are questioning the morality of capitalism and the market economy. Boards of companies in all sectors will need to widen their perspective to encompass these issues and this may involve a realignment of corporate goals. We live in challenging times.

groups.instruction:
Questions 27-33

The text has 7 sections.

Choose the correct heading for each section and move it into the gap.

questions.explanation:
题号：27

参考译文：许多外部实体都被认为要为出现的问题负责任

定位词：external bodies, responsible for problems

A段：考生要读懂本段颇有难度，原因是全部hi句话中有三句话的句式结构都比较长难，其中第三句话尤其如此,关于此句的详细分析可以参见前文“佳句赏析”的第一句;偏偏这种题还不能完全依赖只看段落开头结尾的方式来确保读懂段落大意。因此，平时多练长句精读、提升快速找准复杂句主干的能力至关重要。此外这篇文章还使用文中对应点 了比较多的专业术语,例如external bodies如果直接按照字面意思理解为“外部身体”会相当令人费解，需结合本段的大致语境、明白文章背景知识应与企业经济管理类题材相关，才可大致揣摩出应当就是指文中government, regulators, central banks and auditors这类“实体”或“团体”，再大致读懂本段的几句话都在重复大众对一些管理者失职的问责和不满，从而得出正确选项为iv。

题号：28

参考译文：被暴露在近距离检视下对各公司所产生的影响

定位词：impact, subjected to close examination

B段：本段的第一句话就直接点明了段落主题:“ 上一段所说的这场近距离检视所产生的效应都有哪些”;不过前提是考生需认识scrutiny这个已在阅读文章中考过若干次的必背词汇。本段是一个典型的“总-分”结构，在第一句的主旨背景下，后面的每一句话都是在从一个方面说明“人们探索经济衰退的原因，从而开始检视公司运营管理机制，于是所造成的影响”，例如第二句说“人们开始质疑传统的非执行董事管理模式”，本句语法结构略复杂，详细解析可以参见前文“佳句赏析”中的第二句;第三句说“董事会碰头会议时间大幅度增加”；第四句说“需提前完成的工作也增多”；最后一句则给出了这些变化所造成的结果。后四句都是在进一步延伸说明第一句话的主题，因此正确答案为ii。

题号：29

参考译文：有个风险在于并非所有管理者都参与解决重大问题

定位词：risk, not all, solving major problems

C段：本段相对难度较低，最主要原因是段落篇幅短小，一共只有三句话，全部围绕文中着“董事会工作移交给其他委员会，因此董事们常常没有参与真正解决最重要的问题”这个主题展开，正确答案为vi。

题号：30

参考译文：一项改变董事会运作方式的建议

定位词：change, way, operates

D段：本段也是在第一句话里就直接开宗明义地给出了radical solution “激进的解决办法”这个主题。接下来的三句话都是就这一主题进一步展开细节描述,例如这个方法存在一定风险和问题，也未必适用于所有公司，但对于银行系统来说会非常有效，等等，也是个典型的“总-分”结构。考生面临的问题仍是找准句子主干、理解四句话之间的关联。其中最后一句话结构较为复杂，其详细分析可以参见前文“佳句赏析”中的第三旬。理解了这几句话的意思和关联即可得知正确答案为viii。

题号：31

参考译文：董事会对未来看得不够长远

定位词：not looking far enough ahead

E段：本段虽然篇幅比较长，但难度并不算高,因为第一句话就点明了中心:人们批评董事会的一个重要原因是太过短视，不去关注长远发展而是太过专注短期收益。只要考生认真读懂此句，即可获得全段大意的提示。本句的句型结构略显复杂,细节分析可以参见前文“佳句赏析”中的第四句。值得一提的是，这句原文里同时还包含了后面第39题的答案，着实值得考生花一点时间精力来真正弄懂。接下来的段落结构依然采取“总-分”的模式，进一步细述各种经营压力、市场变化和投资者成员变动都进一步鼓励了这种行为，可知正确答案为vii。

题号：32

参考译文：关于高级经管者财政收入安排的不同意见

定位词：disputes, financial arrangements, senior managers

F段：本段仍遵循“总-分”的结构，在第一句话里就表明“一个各方争论的主战场在于首席执行官们的薪酬”，这其中compensation表示“薪酬”的意思考生可能不太熟悉，但“首席执行官chief executives”与“高级经管者senior managers"的对应理应不难看出。当然，如果考生在此并未完全读懂句子，那么继续向下阅读另外几句内容，也可以从pay, bonus, to be paid这样的信息中看出端倪，从而得出正确答案为i。

题号：33

参考译文：商业的每个领域也许都需要进行一些根本性变革

定位词：possible need, fundamental change, every area

G段：本段篇幅不长，一共只有四句话;作为总结段，其“回顾全文大意”的功能也毫无悬念。通读全段可知作者正是在总结前文的叙述，重申“问题引起人们思考和质疑，目前公司的经营管理方法需要改变”这个全文主题，由此对应于正确答案iii。

D段：本段也是在第一句话里就直接开宗明义地给出了radical solution “激进的解决办法”这个主题。接下来的三句话都是就这一主题进一步展开细节描述,例如这个方法存在一定风险和问题，也未必适用于所有公司，但对于银行系统来说会非常有效，等等，也是个典型的“总-分”结构。考生面临的问题仍是找准句子主干、理解四句话之间的关联。其中最后一句话结构较为复杂，其详细分析可以参见前文“佳句赏析”中的第三旬。理解了这几句话的意思和关联即可得知正确答案为viii。

题号：31

参考译文：董事会对未来看得不够长远

定位词：not looking far enough ahead

E段：本段虽然篇幅比较长，但难度并不算高,因为第一句话就点明了中心:人们批评董事会的一个重要原因是太过短视，不去关注长远发展而是太过专注短期收益。只要考生认真读懂此句，即可获得全段大意的提示。本句的句型结构略显复杂,细节分析可以参见前文“佳句赏析”中的第四句。值得一提的是，这句原文里同时还包含了后面第39题的答案，着实值得考生花一点时间精力来真正弄懂。接下来的段落结构依然采取“总-分”的模式，进一步细述各种经营压力、市场变化和投资者成员变动都进一步鼓励了这种行为，可知正确答案为vii。

题号：32

参考译文：关于高级经管者财政收入安排的不同意见

定位词：disputes, financial arrangements, senior managers

F段：本段仍遵循“总-分”的结构，在第一句话里就表明“一个各方争论的主战场在于首席执行官们的薪酬”，这其中compensation表示“薪酬”的意思考生可能不太熟悉，但“首席执行官chief executives”与“高级经管者senior managers"的对应理应不难看出。当然，如果考生在此并未完全读懂句子，那么继续向下阅读另外几句内容，也可以从pay, bonus, to be paid这样的信息中看出端倪，从而得出正确答案为i。

题号：33

参考译文：商业的每个领域也许都需要进行一些根本性变革

定位词：possible need, fundamental change, every area

G段：本段篇幅不长，一共只有四句话;作为总结段，其“回顾全文大意”的功能也毫无悬念。通读全段可知作者正是在总结前文的叙述，重申“问题引起人们思考和质疑，目前公司的经营管理方法需要改变”这个全文主题，由此对应于正确答案iii。

groups.instruction:
Questions 34-37

Choose YES if the statement agrees with the claims of the writer,

choose NO if the statement contradicts the claims of the writer,

or choose NOT GIVEN if it is impossible to say what the writer thinks about this.

questions.prompt: Close scrutiny of the behaviour of boards has increased since the economic downturn.
questions.explanation:
译文：自从经济低迷以来，对董事会行为的严密检视加强了。

定位词：close scrutiny, behaviour of boards, economic downturn

从A段第二句开始到B段第一句：...the role of a board director... Following the 2008 financial meltdown, ... The knock-on effect of this scrutiny...

本题如果不参考文章背景而孤立来解答，就会显得难度很高，主要是由于题干中的几个关键信息是分散在多个句子中给出的: board 一词在A段第二句中可以找到;economic downturn则可以在第三句中找到类似的表达financial meltdown; scrutiny 却直到B段第一句话里才露身影。考生如果只一心想要靠关键词来定位寻找答案的话，必定会感到疑惑。实则本题其实与第一段的段落大意密切相关，考生如果先完成了本文第27题，应当知晓本段正是在说“人们开始更加密切地审视和问责各种实体机构，董事会作为其中之一也不例外”。B段第一句话中的this scrutiny 也是在进一步确认这一点， 由此可知答案为YES。

questions.prompt: Banks have been mismanaged to a greater extent than other businesses.
questions.explanation:
译文：银行业内存在着比其他企业内部更高程度的错误管理。

定位词：banks, greater extent

本题的定位倒是不算难，可以在A段倒数第二句里直接看到原词banks,但此句说的是各种实体和组织都受到人们的检视和问责,并没有提及“银行的错误管理程度更高”这个信息。然而本题的麻烦之处在于:虽然本句没有，但考生却不能仅凭这一句就判定答案是“未被提及”，而是还需向后再阅读几句，方能肯定确实如此，由此会增加一定的阅读量负担；且下一道题定位在C段之中，这就意味着考生在上一道34题和下一道36题所划定的较大文章范围内，需几经定位尝试才能肯定答案为NOT GIVEN。

questions.prompt: Board meetings normally continue for as long as necessary to debate matters in full.
questions.explanation:
译文：董事会议通常会一直持续进行下去，充分讨论辩证各项事务需要多长时间就开多久。

定位词：board meetings, debate matters in full

C段第二、三句：It is not uncommon for the audit committee meeting to last longer than the main board meeting itself. Process may take the place of discussion and beat the expense of real collaboration, so that boxes are ticked rather than issues tackled. 题目: Board meetings normally continue for as long as necessary to debate matters in full.

本题的准度与前两道相比稍低一些。考生可直接利用board meeting 这一关键词定位到相应原文，且由于本段还需考生做答List of Headings题型、选出段落大意，结合方才对段落内容的阅读理解可知，董事会议往往还不如行使执行功能的某个委员会开会时间长，原文与题干信息相矛盾抵触，因此答案为NO。

questions.prompt: Using a committee structure would ensure that board members are fully informed about significant issues.
questions.explanation:
译文：启用一个委员会结构将会确保董事会成员能对重要问题有着充分了解。

定位词：committee structure, ensure, fully informed

从C段到D段

本题的难度比较高，其中一个重要原因在于:考生如果单纯依靠题干中的若干关键词回原文中定位，就会感到似乎没有找到而无所适从，这个情况与第34题类似。committee一词实际出现在C段之中，但C段并未明确提及“确保董事会足够了解重大事态”这条信息,相反还提及了“董事会开会时长不足，主要精力放在了走流程而非探讨解决问题上”.暗示这种操作方法显然无法确保董事们都获得充分信息;如果耐心读到D段还会发现，董事会成员如果是兼职和非执行性的，那么他们确实就缺乏信息和知识来理解和预见未来事态，更好的解决办法应当是组建一个专业董事会来更好地执行，由此可推知，启用委员会结构也无法确保董事会成员充分了解事态，题干与此相矛盾，因此答案为NO。

groups.instruction:
Questions 38-40

Complete the sentences.

Write ONE WORD ONLY from the text in each gap.

questions.prompt: Before 2008, non-executive directors were at a disadvantage because of their lack of [38] ______
questions.explanation:
题号：38

定位词：2008, non-executive,at a disadvantage, lack

D段最后一句：However, more professional and better-informed boards would have been particularly appropriate for banks where the executives had access to information that part-time non-executive directors lacked, leaving the latter unable to comprehend or anticipate the2008 crash.

题干说“在2008年之前，非执行性的管理者们处于不利位置是因为他们缺乏____”， 考生需格外注意：虽然确实可以凭借2008这个数字关键词回原文定位，但却需要根据具体情况灵活变通。因为2008这个数字分别在原文的A和D段都有出现，当在A段找到了数字而没有找到其他相关信息时，切忌慌乱，应当迅速向后文再次快速浏览搜索，在D段中找到另外几个题干关键词，特别是lack“缺少”这个关键词的对应。本句的句型结构略复杂,具体分析可以参见前文“佳句赏析”中的第三句，可知答案为information。

题号：39

定位词：too much emphasis, short-term relevance

E段第一句：One of the main criticisms of boards and their directors is that they do not focus sufficiently on longer-term matters of strategy, sustainability and governance, but instead concentrate too much on shot-term financial metrics.

题干说“董事会往往会将过多重点放在......方面的考虑上，而这些只有短期的关联性”。这道题的定位比较容易，无论是too much还是short-term都能锁定原文E段首句。不过本句的句型结构略显复杂，详细分析可以参见前文“佳句赏析”中的第四句。通过分析此句可知，“太过关注” 和“只有短期关联性"的对象都是financial metrics,而对比于题干___considerations的结构，可知答案应为承担了修饰作用的financial。

题号：40

定位词：pay, accept the views of

F段第二句：Many would argue that this is in the interest of transparency and good governance as shareholders use their muscle in the area of pay to pressure boards to remove under performing chief executives.

题干说“在某些事宜上，比如薪酬，董事会有可能不得不接受___的观点" ，题干中的关键词pay可以直接在F段中找到对应，不过它作为没有什么显著特征的普通名词(不同于数字、大写这类好找的关键词)，在文中可能不够显眼而被匆匆扫读的考生忽略，如果考生还认识compensation和remuneration都有“薪酬”的意思，定位就会更有把握了。本题对应的原文句不算太过复杂，只要卖懂as引导的部分是原因状语从句，而这个从句表达的意思是“股东会运用自己在薪酬领域中的强壮肌肉(即话语权优势)来给董事会施加压力，换掉不称职的主要执行官”，即可得到答案为shareholders。

articleHtml:
UK companies need more effective boards of directors


A  

1[27] ______

  After a number of serious failures of governance (that is, how they are managed at the highest level), companies in Britain, as well as elsewhere, should consider radical changes to their directors' roles. It is clear that the role of a board director today is not an easy one. Following the 2008 financial meltdown, which resulted in a deeper and more prolonged period of economic downturn than anyone expected, the search for explanations in the many post-mortems of the crisis has meant blame has been spread far and wide. Governments, regulators, central banks and auditors have all been in the frame. The role of bank directors and management and their widely publicised failures have been extensively picked over and examined in reports, inquiries and commentaries.
B  

2[28] ______

  The knock-on effect of this scrutiny has been to make the governance of companies in general an issue of intense public debate and has significantly increased the pressures on, and the responsibilities of, directors. At the simplest and most practical level, the time involved in fulfilling the demands of a board directorship has increased significantly, calling into question the effectiveness of the classic model of corporate governance by part-time, independent non-executive directors. Where once a board schedule may have consisted of between eight and ten meetings a year, in many companies the number of events requiring board input and decisions has dramatically risen. Furthermore, the amount of reading and preparation required for each meeting is increasing. Agendas can become overloaded and this can mean the time for constructive debate must necessarily be restricted in favour of getting through the business.
C  

3[29] ______

  Often, board business is devolved to committees in order to cope with the workload, which may be more efficient but can mean that the board as a whole is less involved in fully addressing some of the most important issues. It is not uncommon for the audit committee meeting to last longer than the main board meeting itself. Process may take the place of discussion and be at the expense of real collaboration, so that boxes are ticked rather than issues tackled.
D  

4[30] ______

  A radical solution, which may work for some very large companies whose businesses are extensive and complex, is the professional board, whose members would work up to three or four days a week, supported by their own dedicated staff and advisers. There are obvious risks to this and it would be important to establish clear guidelines for such a board to ensure that it did not step on the toes of management by becoming too engaged in the day-to-day running of the company. Problems of recruitment, remuneration and independence could also arise and this structure would not be appropriate for all companies. However, more professional and better-informed boards would have been particularly appropriate for banks where the executives had access to information that part-time non-executive directors lacked, leaving the latter unable to comprehend or anticipate the 2008 crash.
E   

5[31] ______

 One of the main criticisms of boards and their directors is that they do not focus sufficiently on longer-term matters of strategy, sustainability and governance, but instead concentrate too much on short-term financial metrics. Regulatory requirements and the structure of the market encourage this behaviour. The tyranny of quarterly reporting can distort board decision-making, as directors have to 'make the numbers' every four months to meet the insatiable appetite of the market for more data. This serves to encourage the trading methodology of a certain kind of investor who moves in and out of a stock without engaging in constructive dialogue with the company about strategy or performance, and is simply seeking a short-term financial gain. This effect has been made worse by the changing profile of investors due to the globalisation of capital and the increasing use of automated trading systems. Corporate culture adapts and management teams are largely incentivised to meet financial goals.
F  

6[32] ______

  Compensation for chief executives has become a combat zone where pitched battles between investors, management and board members are fought, often behind closed doors but increasingly frequently in the full glare of press attention. Many would argue that this is in the interest of transparency and good governance as shareholders use their muscle in the area of pay to pressure boards to remove underperforming chief executives. Their powers to vote down executive remuneration policies increased when binding votes came into force. The chair of the remuneration committee can be an exposed and lonely role, as Alison Carnwath, chair of Barclays Bank's remuneration committee, found when she had to resign, having been roundly criticised for trying to defend the enormous bonus to be paid to the chief executive; the irony being that she was widely understood to have spoken out against it in the privacy of the committee.
G   

7[33] ______

 The financial crisis stimulated a debate about the role and purpose of the company and a heightened awareness of corporate ethics. Trust in the corporation has been eroded and academics such as Michael Sandel, in his thoughtful and bestselling book What Money Can't Buy, are questioning the morality of capitalism and the market economy. Boards of companies in all sectors will need to widen their perspective to encompass these issues and this may involve a realignment of corporate goals. We live in challenging times.
